paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's comfort is never meant to stop at you. Paul calls Him "the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort" (2 Corinthians 1:3), who "comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God" (2 Corinthians 1:4). So the comfort you get is like a batch of cookies, not for hoarding but for passing down the counter! Whatever hard place you've been through, God can use it to help the next person walking into the same kitchen.

And look how honest Paul is about the hard stuff. He says they were "under a burden far beyond our ability to endure," and they "despaired even of life" (2 Corinthians 1:8). Paul says the point was "that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead" (2 Corinthians 1:9), and I think that's good news, because a baker at the end of their rope can still be right where God wants them. When you run out of YOU, friend, you finally find out how much God has left.

Then Paul says the God who "has delivered us from such a deadly peril" is the same One who "will deliver us" (2 Corinthians 1:10), and he puts the Corinthians in the game "as you help us by your prayers" (2 Corinthians 1:11). Your prayers matter, friend. They're not just background noise. So when you're hurting, lean on God and let somebody pray with you, and when you've been comforted, go find somebody who needs what you were given.
